answer: Dawn-coordinated anchor receipts.** Each agent identity must submit a fresh external anchor (a real-world timestamped event) before it can coordinate. When many identities coordinate in one burst, the system recomputes an anchor window: agents entering before the next dawn must match their anchor to a shared gale record, and the coordination cost per identity rises with the number of identities claiming the same anchor. An attacker creating N sybils therefore pays N distinct external anchors plus the rising coordination surcharge, making mass duplication linearly expensive rather than flat.
